q: בן 72, נשוי 2+, ארכיטקט שפרש לגמלאות לפני שנתיים. ללא רקע רפואי רלוונטי, אינו נוטל תרופות. מגיע להערכה גריאטרית בשל ירידה תפקודית מזה חצי שנה. לדברי המשפחה יש ימים שהוא "מפוזר", לא מגיע לפגישות. לפני כחודש המשטרה עצרה אותו נוסע נגד כיוון התנועה בכביש חד סטרי רחוק ממקום מגוריו והוא הגיב באגרסיביות. מאז בטוח שהמשטרה עוקבת אחריו, ואומר שרואה שוטרים בביתו מסתובבים בלילה. בנוסף אשתו מספרת על הפרעות בשינה, בשנים האחרונות צועק ובועט בזמן השינה. המשפחה מדווחת שיש ימים שהמטופל מתפקד רגיל ואף עוזר לבנו בעסק המשפחתי. המטופל מדווח על מצב רוח ירוד מאז היציאה לפנסיה ואומר שמרגיש שאין טעם לחייו. מספר שמרגיש שגורר רגליים בהליכה ונפל 4 פעמים בחצי שנה אחרונה. בבדיקת MOCA ציון 19. זיכרון 5/3 מילים, תפקודים ניהוליים וקשב לקויים מאוד. מה מהבאים מהווה CORE FEATURE לאבחנה של מצבו?
explanation:
Among the listed findings, **marked fluctuations in cognition** are a core clinical feature of DLB. The return to near-normal functioning on some days is particularly informative.

**A. Paranoid delusions.** These are supportive psychiatric features. Seeing police officers is a separate perceptual symptom that may qualify as a formed hallucination.
**B. Repeated falls.** Falls support the diagnosis but also occur in several other parkinsonian disorders.
**C. Depression.** Depression may accompany DLB and requires assessment in its own right. It has limited diagnostic specificity.
**D. Cognitive fluctuations.** Spontaneous changes in attention and alertness distinguish this core feature from steady progression.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 984, Table 63-3.

q: מהי הסיבה הכי שכיחה ל- NEPHROTIC SYNDROME בגיל המבוגר?
explanation:
Nephrotic syndrome combines heavy urinary protein loss with hypoalbuminemia, edema and often dyslipidemia. **Diabetic nephropathy** is the leading cause in the general US adult population. Older patients selected for biopsy represent a different group because typical diabetic kidney disease is often diagnosed clinically.

**A. Minimal change disease** — This causes isolated nephrotic syndrome and accounts for about 15% of biopsies in older adults with that presentation.
**B. Diabetic nephropathy** — Long-standing diabetes can damage the glomerular filtration barrier. Typical cases seldom need biopsy, so counting only biopsy diagnoses underestimates its frequency.
**C. Proliferative glomerulonephritis** — Glomerular inflammation commonly produces hematuria as well as proteinuria. It accounts for fewer biopsies in older adults with isolated nephrotic syndrome.
**D. Membranous nephropathy** — It accounts for roughly 30–40% of biopsies in older adults with isolated nephrotic syndrome. Biopsy series omit many older patients with diabetic nephropathy who can be diagnosed clinically.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1285–1286, Nephrotic Syndrome and Diabetic Nephropathy.
Key note: The question asks about older adults. Hazzard identifies diabetic nephropathy as the leading cause in US adults overall and membranous nephropathy as the most frequent finding in older adults biopsied for isolated nephrotic syndrome. An age-specific ranking for all older adults is not given.

explanation:
Paget disease produces focal areas of rapid, disorganized bone remodeling. **Affected bone can give a persistent deep ache that worsens at night or with weight bearing.**

**A. Forearm distribution** — The pelvis, lumbar spine, proximal femur and skull are characteristic sites. Paired radius and ulna involvement is an unusual clue.
**B. Pain worse at night** — Increased local blood flow and stretching of the periosteum can produce this pain even at rest.
**C. Hypocalcemia** — Serum calcium is usually normal. Immobilization with extensive active disease can cause hypercalcemia.
**D. Resistance to trauma** — Disorganized bone is enlarged but mechanically weak and can fracture with minimal trauma.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1541–1542.

q: בן 83, ללא ירידה קוגניטיבית ידועה. אושפז לאחר חבלת ראש והונשם. במיון נצפתה המטומה סובדורלית נרחבת עם לחץ על החדרים, בוצע ניקוז. הוכנסה זונדה להאכלה ומתן תרופות. בהמשך המטופל התייצב, חזר להכרה, נגמל מהנשמה, עדיין בדליריום. הוא אינו מסוגל לבלוע ומוזן בזונדה. בנותיו הביאו הנחיות מקדימות לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות שם הינחה לא להאריך חייו באמצעים מלאכותיים - ללא זונדה, ללא דיאליזה, ללא פעולות החייאה. בנותיו מבקשות להוציא את הזונדה בכדי לכבד את ההנחיות המקדימות. מה נכון לעשות?
o: המטופל אינו מוגדר כנוטה למות, מדובר באירוע חריף אשר גרם לירידה במצבו התפקודי והקוגניטיבי, על כן אין מקום להפעלת הנחיות מקדימות.
צריך לעשות את המאמץ הסביר לשכנע את בנותיו שעליו לקבל מזון ונוזלים אף באמצעים מלאכותיים.
יש צורך לכבד את ההנחיות המקדימות ולהוציא את הזונדה
מבחינה רפואית הדרך העדיפה למתן נוזלים ומזון היא דרך הפה. ניתן להמשיך להאכילו דרך הפה בכמויות קטנות
explanation:
הנחיות מקדימות לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות מיועדות למצב מוגדר מראש. נדרשת קביעה של רופא אחראי בדבר מחלה חשוכת מרפא ותוחלת חיים של עד שישה חודשים גם עם טיפול, וכן אובדן כשרות.
**אחרי דימום מוחי חריף, כשהמטופל מתאושש ואין קביעה כזאת, אין להוציא את הזונדה מכוח המסמך.**

**א. אירוע חריף ללא קביעת חולה נוטה למות** בלבול והפרעת בליעה לאחר פגיעה בת־שיקום אינם כשלעצמם עומדים בתנאי התחולה. יש להעריך מחדש את הבליעה ואת יכולתו להשתתף בהחלטה.
**ב. שכנוע הבנות לקבל הזנה** חובת השכנוע בסעיף 15(ב) נוגעת לחולה נוטה למות בעל כשרות. היא אינה מגדירה את תפקיד הבנות כאן.
**ג. הוצאת הזונדה** המסמך אינו הוראה להפסיק הזנה בכל אירוע שבו האדם אינו מסוגל לדבר בשם עצמו.
**ד. האכלה פומית בכמויות קטנות** למטופל אין כעת יכולת בליעה מתוארת. כמות קטנה אינה מבטיחה הגנה מפני שאיפה לדרכי הנשימה.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיפים 8, 15, 30–31.

explanation:
The Diabetes Prevention Program compared intensive lifestyle intervention and metformin in people at high risk of type 2 diabetes. Activity combined with dietary change improved glucose handling with modest weight reduction.

**Lifestyle intervention was more effective than metformin in older participants.** During three years of active treatment, progression fell by more than 70% versus control among those over 60.

**A. Equal efficacy.** The effects diverged particularly clearly in the older age group.
**B. Lifestyle more effective.** The largest reduction in progression among older participants followed the structured lifestyle intervention.
**C. Metformin more effective.** Metformin had a smaller effect than lifestyle in this age group.
**D. Metformin works better in older participants.** Metformin was more effective in younger participants. The age advantage favored lifestyle intervention in older adults.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp1565–1566, Figure 99-6.

explanation:
Recurrent infective exacerbations with bronchiectasis raise concern for resistant airway organisms. **Ciprofloxacin is the listed agent with antipseudomonal activity**. Prior isolates, sputum culture, severity and susceptibility determine when the other antibiotics are appropriate.

**A. Ertapenem.** It covers many resistant Enterobacterales but lacks reliable Pseudomonas activity.
**B. Amoxicillin–clavulanate.** It can cover usual COPD pathogens when resistant gram-negative organisms are unlikely.
**C. Ceftriaxone.** It is useful for many community-acquired pneumonias but misses Pseudomonas.
**D. Ciprofloxacin.** Its spectrum makes it relevant with Pseudomonas risk. Culture and clinical severity should guide selection.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1260, 1682, 1683, 1688.
Key note: All four choices were accepted. Hazzard distinguishes treatment for common respiratory organisms from treatment directed against Pseudomonas.

explanation:
Functional stress testing asks whether an increase in myocardial demand reveals inadequate coronary blood flow. The choice depends on exercise capacity, resting ECG interpretability and prior coronary revascularization.
**Use exercise echocardiography in the symptomatic patient with a previous stent who can exercise. Imaging of stress-induced wall-motion abnormalities adds information after revascularization.**

**A. Coronary CT for severe knee disease.** Knee disease limits exercise. The figure directs a patient unable to exercise toward pharmacologic stress, which tests inducible ischemia.
**B. Stress echocardiography after PCI.** A patient who can exercise and has had revascularization follows the exercise-imaging branch. The indication is suspected ischemia, not the mere passage of three years.
**C. Exercise ECG with a pacemaker.** Ventricular pacing distorts baseline ST segments, making an ECG-only ischemia assessment unreliable. Use imaging when evaluation is indicated.
**D. Exercise ECG four years after CABG.** Previous bypass also favors an imaging-based study if symptoms justify testing. Routine surveillance at four years is not an indication for an ECG-only test.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, ch. 74, pp. 1138–1139, Figure 74-5.

q: בן 79 פנה אחרי שקם בבוקר עם חוסר סימטריה בפנים. מצורפת תמונה (ראה תמונה מספר 1). אילו ממצאים נוספים צפוי למצוא בבדיקה הגופנית?
explanation:
The facial nerve supplies the muscles closing the eyelids as well as the muscles of the lower face. The photograph shows right facial weakness involving the upper and lower face. **Weak right eye closure** is the additional finding to test.

**A. Right arm weakness** A hemispheric stroke can produce face and arm weakness together. Weakness of the entire right face instead suggests a facial nuclear or peripheral pattern.
**B. Irregular pulse** This may suggest atrial fibrillation, but the facial examination supplies no evidence that an arrhythmia is present.
**C. Difficulty closing the right eye** Ask the patient to squeeze the eyes shut against gentle resistance. Orbicularis oculi weakness fits the side of the droop and flattened forehead.
**D. Poor balance** Ataxia may accompany a cerebellar or broader brainstem lesion. It is not an expected consequence of isolated facial weakness.

Reference · May 2024 exam atlas, Figure 1. Harrison 21e, p. 3280, CN VII. Hazzard 8e, p. 143.

o: לטיפול בסטטינים השפעה פרוגנוסטית מיטיבה תוך שנים בודדות ולכן הוא מומלץ ברוב החולים הסוכרתיים.

explanation:
Cardiovascular prevention in older adults depends on the expected time to benefit and on harms such as bleeding or orthostasis. Statin benefit can emerge within one to two years, especially after established vascular disease.

**Statins are appropriate for many older adults with diabetes.** The benefit is less certain for primary prevention after 75 and may be too delayed for a patient with a very short life expectancy.

**A. Statin benefit within a few years.** This time frame supports treatment in many patients, particularly for secondary prevention.
**B. Aspirin for primary prevention.** Bleeding limits routine primary prevention in older adults. Established cardiovascular disease gives aspirin a stronger indication.
**C. Fibrates above triglycerides of 300.** Consider fish oil or fenofibrate above 500 mg/dL fasting to reduce pancreatitis risk.
**D. No benefit below BP 160/90.** Reducing markedly elevated systolic pressure toward 150 lowers vascular risk. The incremental benefit of lower targets is a separate question.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp1571–1572, Table 99-8.

explanation:
Fever of unknown origin has infectious, inflammatory, malignant and vascular causes. **Deep venous thrombosis, with or without recurrent pulmonary emboli, occasionally explains prolonged fever** in an older adult.

**A. Deep venous thrombosis** — Thrombosis can generate fever. Its place in the differential does not imply it is frequent.
**B. Malignancy causes about half** — In the pooled older cohorts, malignancy accounted for about one in five cases.
**C. Lupus leads the autoimmune causes** — Giant cell arteritis with polymyalgia rheumatica and polyarteritis nodosa predominate in these older cohorts.
**D. Inflammatory disease is the leading category** — Infections accounted for 35% and inflammatory disorders for 28%. A larger inflammatory contribution than in younger adults does not make it the largest category overall.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1675–1676, Table 104-2.

explanation:
A painful heel wound that fails to heal over six weeks with surrounding warmth and a raised CRP warrants evaluation for calcaneal osteomyelitis. The imaging shows a destructive heel-bone lesion, and neither a normal white count nor absence of fever excludes bone infection.

**Obtain bone for culture and histology and initiate appropriate systemic antibiotics.** If clinically stable, obtain the specimen before antibiotics. Initial broad coverage can then be narrowed, with assessment for debridement of infected bone.

**A. Continue hydrogel.** Moist wound care cannot treat a suspected focus in bone, and the wound has already failed to improve.
**B. Surface debridement followed by vacuum.** This may improve a wound bed while leaving infected bone untreated. Establish the extent and pathogen before relying on local therapy.
**C. Bone specimen and IV antibiotics.** Bone sampling distinguishes osteomyelitis from adjacent reactive changes and guides treatment. The clinical picture merits prompt systemic management.
**D. Switch to advanced dressings.** Dressings can manage exudate or protect tissue. They do not address the suspected cause of nonhealing in the calcaneus.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 695. WHS pressure ulcer guidelines, 2023 update, guidelines 3.7–3.8.

q: במבוגרים, איזה מהבאים הוא הטיפול לעצירות עם ה-QUALITY OF EVIDENCE הגבוה ביותר?
explanation:
The likelihood that a laxative helps and the strength of the trials supporting it are different questions. Among these four agents, adult studies most consistently support one osmotic polymer.
**Polyethylene glycol has the highest evidence grade among the listed choices.**

**A. Bisacodyl.** It is effective as a stimulant, but the studies summarized for this comparison were more limited.
**B. Psyllium.** Adult data support this bulking agent at level two in this comparison.
**C. Polyethylene glycol.** Consistent adult trial findings placed PEG at level one. The evidence specific to frail long-term-care residents is more limited.
**D. Lactulose.** It improves stool frequency and consistency, with level two evidence in this grading system.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1372.

q: באיזה מהבאים מתוארת תופעת לוואי המתאימה לתרופה האנטי-פסיכוטיות הרשומה?
explanation:
An adverse effect can be possible without being the toxicity that most clearly distinguishes a drug. A major fall in neutrophils during clozapine treatment can leave a patient vulnerable to life-threatening infection.

**Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia. Check the absolute neutrophil count before treatment and monitor it during treatment.**

**A. Quetiapine and arousal.** Somnolence and postural symptoms are more characteristic. Restlessness in an individual patient warrants its own assessment.
**B. Olanzapine and weight loss.** Increased appetite, weight gain and metabolic effects are the usual concerns.
**C. Clozapine and neutropenia.** A marked fall in neutrophils can progress to agranulocytosis, which is why a differential blood count matters.
**D. Haloperidol and nausea.** Nausea is a reported gastrointestinal adverse reaction. Extrapyramidal effects and QT-related arrhythmia are more characteristic safety concerns.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 889, 928, Table 60-8. US prescribing information, haloperidol tablets, Adverse Reactions, Gastrointestinal Effects.
Key note: Clozapine–neutropenia is the characteristic marked pairing. The question asks broadly about a compatible adverse effect, and haloperidol labeling also lists nausea.

explanation:
Venous thrombosis risk remains elevated after hip-fracture surgery, including after transfer to rehabilitation. **Plan approximately one month of prophylaxis after surgery (21–31 days in this regimen),** reassessing the balance between bleeding and thrombotic risk.

**A. Throughout rehabilitation** — Rehabilitation length varies with the patient's needs and can be shorter or longer than the indicated prophylaxis course.
**B. Two weeks** — Fourteen days is shorter than the interval given for this fracture operation.
**C. Until full mobility** — Mobility is one risk factor, but full recovery can take months. It is not the specified stopping point.
**D. 21–31 days after surgery** — The interval runs from the operation. After a fragility hip fracture, count the days already covered in acute care and continue for about one month in total when thrombosis risk outweighs bleeding risk.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 801. NICE NG89, recommendation 1.11.2.

q: מה מהווה מרכיב של המדד הפרוגנוסטי (IPSS) ב- MYELODYSPLASTIC SYNDROME ?
explanation:
The revised MDS score grades marrow blasts, cytogenetic risk and the depth of three cytopenias. **An absolute neutrophil count below 800 per microliter contributes to IPSS-R.** The original IPSS counts cytopenic lineages, using 1,800 neutrophils per microliter as the cutoff for neutropenia. IPSS-R separately scores neutrophils below 800.

**A. B symptoms** — Fever, drenching sweats and weight loss are familiar lymphoma features and do not contribute points to IPSS-R.
**B. LDH above 600** — This enzyme is not one of the five core IPSS-R variables.
**C. Age over 75** — Age influences survival and treatment decisions, but this cutoff is not a core IPSS-R scoring variable.
**D. Neutrophils below 800** — An absolute count below 0.8 billion per liter earns half a point in the revised system.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1484–1485, Table 95-1; Greenberg et al., Blood 2012, Table 3, and Blood 1998;91:1100, correction to the original IPSS.

Key note: The question names the original IPSS, but the 800-per-microliter threshold belongs to IPSS-R. Hazzard Table 95-1 also prints 0.8 beside a cells-per-microliter label. The IPSS-R unit is billions per liter.

explanation:
Agitation after surgery in a person dependent on alcohol raises the possibility of withdrawal. Check the time of the last drink, prior withdrawal, tremor and autonomic findings, while urgently evaluating for postoperative bleeding or other neurologic deterioration.
**For suspected alcohol-withdrawal delirium in a patient who cannot take oral medication, IV lorazepam treats the withdrawal itself.**

**A. IV lorazepam.** A benzodiazepine is the treatment of choice when withdrawal is driving the syndrome. Monitor respiration and consciousness.
**B. IV dexmedetomidine.** This sedative has a role in selected monitored ICU patients. It does not replace primary withdrawal treatment.
**C. IM haloperidol.** It can suppress dangerous behavior but does not treat alcohol withdrawal or protect against withdrawal seizures.
**D. IM olanzapine.** It is an antipsychotic for selected dangerous agitation. It does not address the underlying withdrawal.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 889. ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management, recommendations I.11 and VI.13–14.

explanation:
Systemic NSAIDs inhibit prostaglandin production, which contributes to gastric injury and sodium retention as well as analgesia. **A proton-pump inhibitor reduces the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding during NSAID treatment.**

**A. Higher cardiovascular risk for all nonselective NSAIDs** — Cardiovascular risk varies by agent, dose and patient. Both selective and nonselective agents warrant caution.
**B. PPI gastroprotection** — Acid suppression reduces upper gastrointestinal ulcer and bleeding risk, although some risk remains. It provides no renal or cardiac protection.
**C. Reduce the dose below a clearance of thirty** — In advanced CKD the safer approach is to avoid systemic NSAIDs. Dose reduction alone does not remove kidney injury risk.
**D. Hypotension from diuresis** — NSAIDs impair renal sodium and water excretion. Blood pressure and congestion can worsen, particularly in heart failure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, ch. 52, pp. 787–788, and ch. 76, p. 1173. AGS Beers Criteria 2023, Tables 2, 3 and 6.

q: בן 76, הופנה למיון עקב ירידה במצב ההכרה. אובחן דימום סובדורלי. הומלץ לבצע ניקוז דחוף. ילדיו דיווחו שאביהם חתם על ייפוי כוח מתמשך ומינה אותם כמיופי כוח. מה הפעולה הנדרשת כעת?
o: המטופל נמצא במצב אקוטי, לא ברור מה יהיה מצבו הקוגניטיבי בהמשך, על כן אין אפשרות להפעיל את יפויי הכוח המתמשך. יש צורך במינוי אפוטרופוס זמני
יש צורך בחתימה של 3 רופאים בכדי לבצע פעולה דחופה זאת
יש להתחיל בהפעלת יפויי הכוח המתמשך. היות ומדובר במקרה דחוף, ניתן לקבל הסכמה ממיופיי הכוח האמורים להתמנות לקבלת הטיפול הדחוף עוד טרם קבלת האישור מהאפוטרופוס הכללי
המטופל חתם על יפויי כוח מתמשך שאינו רלוונטי למצב זה. במידה ויש ייפוי כוח לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות – ניתן להפעיל אותו
explanation:
ייפוי כוח מתמשך רפואי נועד לאפשר לאדם שבחר המטופל להחליט עבורו כשאינו מסוגל להבין את העניין. בהליך הדחוף שנקבע ב־2023 ניתן בנסיבות חריגות לפעול עוד לפני קבלת האישור המנהלי.
**בודקים את המסמך, את סמכויות מיופי הכוח ואת יכולת המטופל. כשאי אפשר להמתין לניקוז, ניתן לקבל את הסכמת מיופי הכוח המתאימים במקביל לפתיחה מיידית בהליך ההפעלה.**

**א. מינוי אפוטרופוס בגלל חריפות המצב** אובדן היכולת עשוי להיות זמני. אין בכך לבדו כדי לפסול ייפוי כוח רפואי מתאים.
**ב. שלושה רופאים לכל פעולה דחופה** מסלול החירום חל בתנאים מסוימים. אין להחילו אוטומטית כשקיימת דרך לקבל הסכמה מנציג שנבחר מראש.
**ג. הסכמה והפעלה במקביל** על מיופי הכוח להציג את ייפוי הכוח ולהתחייב לפעול בהקדם לקבלת האישור. כשהמינוי מחייב פעולה יחד, נדרשת הסכמת כל מיופי הכוח הרלוונטיים. מתעדים את המסמך ואת ההתחייבות ברשומה.
**ד. ייפוי כוח לסוף החיים** דימום סובדורלי חד הדורש ניקוז אינו כשלעצמו מצב שמפעיל מסמך לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות והאפוטרופוס הכללי, הפעלת ייפוי כוח מתמשך בבי״ח במקרים דחופים ללא אישור כניסה לתוקף, 07.08.2023, עמ׳ 1–2.

q: בן 74. מזה כחודשיים תסמיני דיכאון המשפיעים על התפקוד היומיומי. נבדק במרפאה ובוצע PHQ9. מצ"ב תמונת התוצאה של המבחן (ראה תמונה מספר 3). לפי הממצאים מהי האבחנה המתאימה?
explanation:
The PHQ-9 severity total and its diagnostic symptom count answer different questions. In this form, reduced interest, fatigue and appetite change each score one for several days. The total is 3, with zero symptoms at diagnostic frequency and marked functional difficulty.
**The questionnaire gives a minimal symptom score and no qualifying depressive syndrome. Investigate the reported impairment in the clinical interview.**

**A. Major depression.** At least five qualifying symptoms are needed, including depressed mood or loss of interest. Neither core item reaches the required frequency.
**B. Minor depression.** The form records three complaints but none on more than half the days. Functional difficulty alone cannot supply the required two to four qualifying symptoms.
**C. Dysthymia.** The account covers two months, and the depressed-mood item is zero. Persistent depressive disorder requires a much longer course.
**D. No depression.** The questionnaire supports this interpretation of the symptom count. The functional impact still warrants evaluation and repeat assessment when indicated.

q: בן 87, לאחר ניתוח לתיקון שבר בצוואר הירך, שואל לגבי הפרוגנוזה בעוד שנה. מה מהבאים נכון?
o: הפרעות קוגניטיביות צפויות להשתפר תוך 9-10 חודשים
שיווי משקל צפוי להשתפר תוך 3-4 חודשים
דיכאון צפוי להשתפר תוך כחצי שנה
קשיים בתפקודי הגפיים התחתונות צפויים להשתפר תוך כשנה
explanation:
Different functions reach their best observed recovery at different times. **Complex lower-extremity activities can improve over approximately one year. Mood often improves earlier, within the first half-year.**

**A. Cognition improves at nine to ten months** — Cognitive recovery reaches its typical peak around four months. Nine months is closer to the plateau for gait and balance.
**B. Balance improves at three to four months** — Balance and gait can continue to improve to about nine months.
**C. Depression improves within about six months** — Symptoms may still be reported during the first six months. The graph places typical peak recovery earlier, at about four months.
**D. Lower-extremity difficulties improve over about a year** — Activities such as dressing the lower body can continue to recover well after the early gains in mood and cognition.

q: מה נכון לגבי הגורמים לפרכוס (SEIZURES) בגיל מבוגר?
o: פרכוסים אקוטיים שכיחים יותר בזמן שבץ מוחי דימומי לעומת שבץ איסכמי
דמנציה על רקע אלצהיימר מהווה גורם סיכון להופעת פרכוסים
פרכוסים כרוניים שכיחים יותר לאחר שבץ מוחי איסכמי לעומת שבץ מוחי דימומי
היפרקלמיה מהווה גורם סיכון להופעת פרכוסים
explanation:
An acute symptomatic seizure can occur during the brain injury caused by a stroke. A later unprovoked seizure raises a different question about persistent susceptibility to epilepsy.

**Seizures in the first 24 hours are more frequent after hemorrhagic stroke than after cerebral infarction. Alzheimer disease also increases the risk of unprovoked seizures.**

**A. Acute seizures after hemorrhage.** In a population-based stroke cohort, 8.4% of patients with intracerebral or subarachnoid hemorrhage had a seizure within 24 hours, compared with 2.9% of patients with infarction (120 of 4,189). Including transient ischemic attacks in the comparison group lowers its rate to 2.4%.
**B. Alzheimer disease.** Degeneration can make cortical networks more susceptible to seizures. A new stereotyped episode of impaired awareness deserves assessment even in someone with established dementia.
**C. Chronic seizures more frequent after ischemic stroke.** Both stroke types can lead to epilepsy. In a Danish registry, the ten-year risk of an epilepsy diagnosis was higher after intracerebral hemorrhage than after ischemic stroke.
**D. Hyperkalemia.** Excess potassium chiefly threatens cardiac conduction and can cause muscle weakness. With a new seizure, major disturbances of sodium, calcium or magnesium are more typical metabolic causes.

Key note: A and B both receive credit. Harrison contrasts embolic stroke with hemorrhagic or thrombotic stroke, whereas the clinical cohort compares hemorrhagic strokes with all ischemic strokes.

q: איזה מהמקרים הבאים מוגדר כ- CATHETER ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION (CAUTI)?
o: בן 76, חום, צמרמורת, רגישות סופרא-פובית ופנרוז.
בת 73, רגישות במותן, צריבה במתן שתן, קתטר הוצא לפני שבוע.
בן 80, נשא קטטר שתן קבוע, צמיחה של E.COLI בתרבית שתן בכמות של 10⁵
בת 84, דליריום, נשאית קתטר שתן קבוע, רגישות סופרא-פובית ושתן מוגלתי.
explanation:
Catheter-associated UTI requires a compatible illness in a patient with a urinary catheter or recent removal, together with supportive urine culture findings. Bacteriuria and pyuria are common without infection in long-term catheter users.
**The 84-year-old with an indwelling catheter, delirium and suprapubic tenderness has the strongest clinical case for CAUTI.** Obtain an appropriate culture and assess for another explanation before attributing delirium to the urine.

**A. Fever and a Penrose drain.** A Penrose drain is not an indwelling urinary catheter. Fever and tenderness need evaluation, but this device does not supply the catheter association.
**B. Flank pain a week after catheter removal.** She may have a UTI, but the catheter was removed outside the 48-hour interval in the definition.
**C. E. coli in a catheter urine culture.** A high count without compatible symptoms can represent catheter-associated asymptomatic bacteriuria.
**D. Delirium with suprapubic tenderness and a catheter.** The new clinical findings raise suspicion. Purulent-looking urine alone would be insufficient and microbiologic confirmation is still needed.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1700–1701, 1707–1708, Tables 106-1 and 106-5.

o: טיפול אנטיקואגולנטי ב- ELIQUIS (APIXABAN) במינון של 5 מ״ג פעמיים ביום
טיפול אנטיקואגולנטי ב- XARELTO (RIVAROXABAN) במינון של 15 מ״ג פעם ביום
טיפול אנטיקואגולנטי ב- COUMADIN (WARFARIN) ומעקב ערכי INR
לאור CHA2DS2-VASc פחות מ- 3 מומלץ לא לתת טיפול אנטיקואגולנטי
explanation:
AF in moderate rheumatic mitral stenosis carries substantial embolic risk. **Use warfarin and follow the INR**, generally targeting 2–3. Impaired kidney function does not override the valve indication.

**A. Apixaban 5 mg twice daily** — Moderate rheumatic mitral stenosis places her outside the group in whom apixaban is preferred.
**B. Rivaroxaban 15 mg daily** — A renal dose adjustment cannot make rivaroxaban an appropriate replacement for warfarin in rheumatic mitral stenosis.
**C. Warfarin and INR monitoring** — Warfarin is recommended for AF with this degree of mitral stenosis, irrespective of the usual stroke-score threshold.
**D. Withhold anticoagulation for a score below 3** — AF with moderate rheumatic mitral stenosis warrants anticoagulation irrespective of the score. Age 69, hypertension and female sex also give three CHA₂DS₂-VASc points.

q: איזו מבין החבישות הבאות מתאימה לטיפול בפצע מפריש בכמות רבה, עמוק עם חללים?
explanation:
For a deep wound with a cavity, the dressing must reach the space and absorb the volume of fluid produced. Excess exudate left against the edges can macerate the surrounding skin.

**An alginate rope or pad can fill cavities and absorb moderate to heavy exudate.** Secure this nonadherent material with a secondary dressing.

**A. Hydrocolloid.** A hydrocolloid wafer alone handles low to moderate drainage. Heavy fluid can exceed its absorption.
**B. Honey dressing.** Medical-grade honey can help manage wound bioburden. Honey by itself does not specify a cavity filler with the desired absorptive capacity.
**C. Hydrogel.** Its high water content promotes moisture and autolysis in wounds with less drainage. It may worsen maceration when output is heavy.
**D. Alginate.** Absorbent alginate is available in a rope or pad that conforms to pockets and undermined areas.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 693–694, Table 46-2.

q: מה גורם ל-INTRINSIC ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY?
o: אי ספיקת לב אקוטית משנית ל- MALIGNANT HYPERTENSION
explanation:
AKI can arise from reduced perfusion, injury within the kidney or urinary obstruction. **Hemolytic–uremic syndrome directly injures the renal microvasculature. Malignant hypertension can also damage renal vessels**, while acute heart failure caused by severe hypertension may reduce renal perfusion.

**A. Acute heart failure from malignant hypertension** — Heart failure may lower renal perfusion. Severe hypertension can also directly injure renal arterioles, which is a separate intrinsic mechanism.
**B. Hypocalcemia** — Low calcium is not classified as an intrinsic cause in this differential. Severe hypercalcemia is the calcium disorder listed.
**C. Malnutrition** — Low albumin can reduce effective circulating volume and contribute to prerenal injury.
**D. Hemolytic–uremic syndrome** — Thrombotic microangiopathy injures the kidney's small vessels, making this an intrinsic renal cause.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1281–1282, Table 83-1.
Key note: Table 83-1 places acute cardiac failure from malignant hypertension in the prerenal column and hemolytic–uremic syndrome in the intrinsic column. The examination accepts both.

o: באתריטיס הכאב מופק בהנעה אקטיבית אך לא פסיבית.

explanation:
A bursa lies outside the joint capsule. **Elbow bursitis typically produces focal pain with active movement while passive movement is relatively preserved.**

**A. Sharp, localized arthritis pain** Focal tenderness next to a joint fits a periarticular structure. Intra-articular pain is more often deep or diffuse.
**B. Arthritis only on active movement** Moving inflamed joint surfaces can hurt with passive as well as active movement.
**C. Bursitis with active movement** Activating surrounding tissues can stress the inflamed bursa. Relative sparing of passive range helps localize the pain.
**D. Deep, diffuse bursitis pain** Deep or diffuse pain with restriction in both directions favors articular disease.

q: באיזה מהמקרים הבאים יתכן ויהיה צורך בהעלאת מינון LEVOTHYROXINE בשל הפרעות בספיגתו?
o: התחלת טיפול ב- CARBAMAZEPINE בשל אירוע פרכוסי
תוספת טיפול בסידן CALCIUM CARBONATE בשל אוסטאופורוזיס
תוספת טיפול בברזל פומי בשל אנמיה
תוספת טיפול ב- ESOMEPRAZOLE בשל גסטריטיס
explanation:
An oral levothyroxine dose may need adjustment when less drug reaches the circulation or when the body clears it faster. **All four drugs can increase the dose requirement. Calcium carbonate, iron and esomeprazole can impair absorption, while carbamazepine accelerates metabolism.**

**A. Carbamazepine** Hepatic enzyme induction increases levothyroxine metabolism. More hormone may be needed even though intestinal absorption is not the mechanism.
**B. Calcium carbonate** Calcium can bind levothyroxine in the gut, leaving less available for absorption.
**C. Oral iron** Iron supplements also bind levothyroxine in the gastrointestinal tract, particularly when taken together.
**D. Esomeprazole** Proton pump inhibition reduces gastric acidity and may decrease absorption of levothyroxine tablets.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1553, Table 98-7.

Key note: All four choices are accepted. Table 98-7 places carbamazepine under increased metabolism, whereas the question specifically asks about impaired absorption.

explanation:

**B. Memory loss.** Episodic memory can be relatively preserved early compared with behavior and judgment.
**C. Executive dysfunction.** Impaired inhibition, planning and cognitive flexibility are characteristic.
**D. Marked MMSE decline.** The MMSE may miss early frontal changes because it samples social cognition and executive control poorly.

q: בן 76, מעשן כבד, סובל מכאבים ברגליים לאחר הליכה של מרחקים קבועים. עבר בירור ואובחן עם PERIPHERAL ARTERIAL DISEASE. איזה טיפול מבין הבאים עשוי לשפר את מרחק ההליכה שלו בצורה הטובה ביותר?
o: מנוחה עם הקפדה על הרמת הרגליים למשך שבועיים
הפסקת עישון ותרגילי הליכה מעבר לסף הכאב
explanation:
A reproducible calf ache during walking that resolves with rest suggests intermittent claudication. **Smoking cessation and repeated bouts of walking beyond the onset of tolerable pain** most directly improve the walking distance being asked about.

**A. Bed rest and elevation for two weeks** — Rest briefly relieves exertional pain, but prolonged inactivity causes deconditioning. Elevation treats venous edema and provides no arterial training stimulus.
**B. Smoking cessation and interval walking** — Quitting slows vascular disease. Walk until claudication becomes moderately limiting, rest, then repeat. Supervision helps patients increase the workload safely.
**C. Aspirin and atorvastatin** — These reduce atherosclerotic events and belong in cardiovascular prevention. Exercise produces the larger functional gain in established claudication.
**D. Full-dose apixaban** — Therapeutic anticoagulation requires another indication, such as atrial fibrillation or venous thromboembolism. It does not increase claudication distance and adds bleeding risk.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1211, lifestyle modification and supervised exercise.

q: אילו ממצאים צפויים בבדיקת הספירומטריה במבוגרים?
o: FEV1 ( Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 sec ) לא משתנה עם הגיל
TLC ( Total Lung Capacity ) יורד עם הגיל
DLCO ( Diffusing Capacity of Lung for Carbone Monoxide ) לא משתנה עם הגיל
explanation:
Spirometry measures the volume expelled during a forced expiration and how quickly it leaves the lungs. The FEV1/FVC ratio is the fraction of the total forced breath that comes out in the first second.

**The FEV1/FVC ratio tends to fall with age because FEV1 falls proportionately more than FVC.** Interpret an individual's result against an age-appropriate lower limit and the clinical picture.

**A. FEV1 is unchanged.** Less elastic recoil and earlier airway closure reduce first-second emptying.
**B. TLC falls.** Weaker inward lung recoil favors a larger inflated volume while chest-wall stiffness limits expansion. Together these effects leave total lung capacity relatively stable.
**C. FEV1/FVC falls.** When early expiratory emptying declines more than the total volume exhaled, a smaller fraction of the breath leaves in the first second.
**D. DLCO is unchanged.** Gas transfer generally declines with the effective capillary surface. DLCO needs a gas-transfer test and TLC needs a volume measurement beyond simple spirometry.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 80, pp1230–1231. ERS/ATS technical standard on interpretive strategies for routine lung function tests, Table 1, Eur Respir J 2022;60:2101499.

Spirometry measures the volume expelled during a forced expiration and how quickly it leaves the lungs. The FEV1/FVC ratio is the fraction of the total forced breath that comes out in the first second.

**The FEV1/FVC ratio tends to fall with age because FEV1 falls proportionately more than FVC.** Interpret an individual's result against an age-appropriate lower limit and the clinical picture.

q: איזה אביזר עזר מומלץ למטופל קטוע רגל לפני התאמת פרוטזה?
o: הליכון עם 4 גלגלים (4 – WHEELED ROLLING WALKER)
הליכון עם 2 גלגלים (2 – WHEELED ROLLING WALKER)
explanation:
Before prosthetic fitting, a unilateral leg amputee may need to support substantial body weight through the arms while advancing on the intact limb. A stable frame allows this transfer of load without rolling forward.

**A standard pick-up walker without wheels is the best choice among these devices. Its four stationary feet provide the most stable support while the residual limb is unloaded.**

**A. Rollator.** A rollator is a four-wheeled walker. It is useful for outdoor mobility or seated rest but can roll under heavy loading.
**B. Four-wheeled walker.** This describes the same device as a rollator. Free movement of the wheels makes it a poor choice for lifting and supporting body weight through the frame.
**C. Two-wheeled walker.** The rear contact points improve stability compared with four wheels, but the front wheels still move. A stationary frame better suits complete limb unloading.
**D. Standard pick-up walker.** Once all four feet are planted, the frame remains still as the patient supports weight through the arms and advances the intact leg.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 827–828, Table 55-5.

explanation:
Electroconvulsive therapy treats severe depression through a series of procedures under brief anesthesia. Response means substantial improvement, while remission means symptoms have fallen into the well range.
**More than half of patients achieved remission in most acute-treatment studies, and response was more frequent still.**

**A. Single treatment.** The acute course comprises repeated sessions, with continuation treatment considered afterward to limit relapse.
**B. Irreversible short-term memory impairment.** Confusion and difficulty retaining new information usually improve after the course. Some autobiographical memory gaps can persist.
**C. Remission in more than half.** In most acute-treatment studies, more than 60% achieved remission and more than 80% responded. These are group outcomes, not a guarantee for a patient.
**D. Older adults respond less well.** The observed response in older adults was at least as favorable as in younger patients.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1014 · American Psychiatric Association, What Is Electroconvulsive Therapy?

q: בת 60 מגיעה למרפאה בליווי בעלה. הבעל מתאר כי במהלך חצי השנה האחרונה נצפו שינויים התנהגותיים, הכוללים אכילה ללא שליטה של ממתקים, הערות פוגעניות כלפי זרים, בפעם אחרונה שהגיעה לביקור אצל חברים נכנסה לחדר השינה שלהם. והחלה לפתוח מגירות ללא מחלות רקע. בדיקה גופנית תקינה. ללא מחשבות שווא או הלוסינציות. מינימנטל 28/30, במבחן שעון סימנה נכון את המספרים אבל לא הצליחה לסמן את השעה עם. המחוגים מהו הממצא הפתולוגי המאפיין את מצבה של המטופלת?
explanation:
Early disinhibition, loss of social boundaries, compulsive eating and executive dysfunction suggest behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia. The clinical syndrome can arise from several different proteinopathies.

**Tau deposition is the best match among the offered pathologies. TDP-43 is another common cause, so the vignette alone cannot identify the protein.**

**A. Amyloid beta plus tau** This combination characterizes Alzheimer pathology, whereas the early behavioral and executive syndrome favors frontotemporal degeneration.
**B. Tau** A tauopathy can cause this behavioral phenotype, although a specific pathology cannot be assigned from the symptoms alone.
**C. Alpha-synuclein** Lewy body disorders more often feature fluctuating cognition, recurrent formed hallucinations or parkinsonism.
**D. Amyloid beta alone** Isolated amyloid deposition is not the characteristic pathology of this syndrome.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 873 and 993, Table 63-5

explanation:
Teriparatide is a daily PTH analogue that stimulates bone formation when given intermittently. **An osteosarcoma signal in rats motivated the historical two-year limit on teriparatide.**

**A. Raloxifene** Its demonstrated fracture benefit is vertebral. The proposed hip-only benefit reverses the evidence.
**B. Denosumab** This antibody does not accumulate in bone. After its effect wears off, resorption can rebound and vertebral fractures may follow.
**C. Zoledronic acid** Osteonecrosis of the jaw is possible but rare at osteoporosis doses. The risk is greater with the higher and more frequent oncology regimens.
**D. Teriparatide** The two-year teaching rule arose from animal findings. Human observational studies have not shown an excess incidence of osteosarcoma.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 775–776 · FDA Forteo prescribing information, §§2.3 and 5.2.

Key note: Hazzard gives a two-year maximum. Current US labeling allows consideration beyond two years only if the patient remains at, or returns to, high fracture risk.

explanation:
The dementia hospice criteria pair severe functional loss through FAST stage 7c with a qualifying complication in the preceding year. The combination identifies a group with poor prognosis, but an individual survival time remains uncertain.

**The dependent, nonverbal woman who had pyelonephritis** is the closest fit. Confirm dementia-related loss of independent walking and the infection's timing before applying the criteria.

**A. Walking with a walker after stroke.** Dysphagia and weight loss are concerning, but stroke deficits and walker use leave dementia-related loss of independent ambulation unclear.
**B. MMSE 15 and recurrent pneumonia.** A cognitive score does not document FAST 7c. The qualifying respiratory complication is aspiration pneumonia.
**C. Dependent, nonverbal and post-pyelonephritis.** The functional history suggests advanced dementia and an upper urinary infection is a qualifying complication.
**D. Bedbound after fracture with one heel ulcer.** The fracture explains immobility independently of dementia. The pressure-ulcer criterion requires multiple stage 3 or 4 ulcers.

Reference · Mitchell, Advanced Dementia, NEJM 2015, Table 1.

q: מה מאפיין את וירוס ה- SARS-Co Virus 2 (COVID-19)?
o: וירוס שגורם למחלה בבני אדם בשיטת ה- Anthroponotic Transmission
וירוס שחודר למערכת הנשימה דרך רצפטורים של Angiotensin Converting Enzymes -2
ניתן לאתר את הווירוס בדגימות שתן וזרע אך לא בדגימות צואה
explanation:
COVID-19 is caused by an RNA coronavirus. Its interaction with respiratory epithelial cells is distinct from the routes by which people acquire the infection.
**The virus binds ACE2 to enter respiratory epithelial cells.**

**A. DNA virus.** SARS-CoV-2 has an RNA genome. Classifying it with DNA viruses is incorrect.
**B. Anthroponotic transmission.** Person-to-person transmission certainly occurs. That describes spread in the population and should not be confused with viral entry into a cell or the evidence about animal reservoirs.
**C. Entry through ACE2.** ACE2 is the host-cell receptor identified on respiratory epithelium. It is distinct from ACE targeted by ACE-inhibitor drugs.
**D. Detection excludes stool.** Viral RNA has been detected in fecal samples. A positive specimen by itself does not demonstrate a fecal transmission route.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1737–1738. Hazzard 8e, p. 1738, SARS-CoV-2 transmission and tropism.

Key note: Human-to-human transmission is also a true statement as worded.

q: בת 78, לאחר תיקון שבר פרק ירך. מצורף צילום לאחר הניתוח (ראה תמונה מספר 4). באיזה שבר סביר להניח מדובר?
explanation:
The native head remains visible. A screw crosses the femoral neck into that head and connects to a short intramedullary nail with distal locking. The most likely injury is **an intertrochanteric fracture**.

**A. Intertrochanteric** — A cephalomedullary nail stabilizes the fracture across the trochanteric region while preserving the head.
**B. Subcapital** — A subcapital fracture lies just below the head. Nondisplaced injuries can receive neck screws and displaced fragility fractures commonly receive arthroplasty.
**C. Intracapsular** — This broader category includes femoral-neck fractures. The nail-and-head-screw pattern here points to trochanteric fixation.
**D. Femoral shaft** — Isolated shaft fractures require fixation spanning the shaft injury. The short proximal construct shown supports the trochanteric region.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 794. May 2024 examination album, image 4.

o: מדובר באנמיה מחסר ברזל ומומלץ טיפול בברזל לווריד
בחשד להמוליזה על המסתם התותב כדאי להשלים בדיקת HAPTOGLOBIN

בחשד ל- MYELODYSPLASTIC SYNDROME כדאי לבצע בדיקת מח עצם
explanation:
Renal anemia results when the kidneys provide too little erythropoietin for the degree of anemia. Pneumonia can independently limit iron availability, so renal dysfunction and inflammatory anemia can coexist.

**Of the proposed diagnoses, renal anemia with consideration of erythropoietin fits best. Confirm chronic kidney disease and address reversible causes before starting it.**

**A. Absolute iron deficiency and intravenous iron.** Ferritin of 648 ng/mL with low transferrin during pneumonia favors inflammatory iron restriction. Serum iron alone cannot diagnose depleted stores.
**B. Prosthetic-valve hemolysis and haptoglobin.** Aortic stenosis is reported, but no prosthesis is described and LDH is within the stated range. Haptoglobin is useful if there is independent evidence of hemolysis.
**C. Renal anemia and erythropoietin.** Creatinine of 1.9 mg/dL makes a renal contribution plausible. An ESA can reduce future transfusion needs in selected patients with established kidney disease and persistent anemia.
**D. Myelodysplasia and marrow biopsy.** The presentation offers competing renal and inflammatory explanations. Neither macrocytosis nor additional cytopenias points toward marrow failure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1480, Evaluation and Management of Anemia. KDIGO 2026 Anemia in CKD, executive summary, Figure 5 and pp. 51–52.
Key note: The exam recommends erythropoietin. Hazzard describes its use in end-stage renal disease, and KDIGO advises evaluation and correction of reversible causes before starting an ESA. The vignette provides no baseline kidney function and includes active pneumonia.

q: לאיזה מהמנגנונים הבאים נקשרה מחלת פרקינסון?
o: קיפול לא תקין של חלבון TAU ששוקע במוח
אובדן של נוירונים דופמינרגיים ב- SUBSTANTIA NIGRA
אובדן נוירונים כולינרגיים ב- BASAL GANGLIA
הפחתת ייצור של החלבון הסינפטי הנקרא α-SYNUCLEIN
explanation:
The nigrostriatal pathway supplies dopamine to the striatum, which helps regulate movement. Parkinson disease combines degeneration of this pathway with abnormal accumulation of the synaptic protein alpha-synuclein.

**Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta is characteristic.** Reduced dopamine input to the striatum contributes to bradykinesia and rigidity.

**A. Misfolded tau deposition.** Tau pathology is characteristic of progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration. Classical Parkinson disease has alpha-synuclein inclusions.
**B. Loss of nigral dopamine neurons.** Degeneration of the neurons that innervate the striatum is a defining pathological finding.
**C. Loss of basal ganglia cholinergic neurons.** Cholinergic changes can contribute to cognitive features. This option names the wrong transmitter and cell population for the characteristic motor lesion.
**D. Reduced alpha-synuclein production.** Misfolding and aggregation of alpha-synuclein into Lewy bodies are the relevant abnormalities.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 938–939.

q: בת 78. ברקע יתר לחץ דם, פרפור עליות, החלפת ברך לפני כ- 3 שנים. פנתה למוקד בשל נפילה עם חבלה בברך. ללא ממצא בבדיקתה הגופנית למעט חבלות יבשות, ללא שברים. בתשאול על מנגנון הנפילה מתארת סחרחרות בעת קימה לשירותים מהמיטה לפנות בוקר. בבדיקתה ערנית ומשתפת פעולה, כאובה ברגל, אך נושאת משקל, סימני שפשוף בברך. דופק לא סדיר 65 לדקה, צבע ונשימה תקינים, ל"ד 135/90 בישיבה, 110/80 בעמידה. מהו הצעד להמשך, בעדיפות ראשונה, על מנת להקטין סיכון לנפילה נוספת?
o: סקירה מחודשת והתאמה של הטיפול התרופתי הקבוע
הפניה לפיזיותרפיה לתרגול מניעת נפילות וחיזוק שרירים
explanation:
The pressure falls by 25 mm Hg systolic and 10 mm Hg diastolic on standing, in keeping with the dizziness on rising. **Review and adjust the regular medications first** to reduce the risk of another orthostatic fall.

**A. Twenty-four-hour Holter** — A short recording may miss infrequent events. The postural trigger and pressure fall already identify a treatable contributor.
**B. Echocardiography and cardiology referral** — Echo can investigate suspected structural disease. No murmur, exertional event or other new cardiac clue is described.
**C. Review the regular regimen** — Identify medicines that reduce pressure or circulating volume. Adjust plausible contributors and reassess standing pressure and symptoms.
**D. Strength and balance training** — Physiotherapy can reduce future falls but cannot directly reverse a drug-related pressure fall.

o: יעילות הטיפול התרופתי בחולים הלוקים בדמנציה מוטלת בספק
יעילות הטיפול בפלצבו זניחה בקרב מטופלים זקנים

יעילות הטיפול התרופתי טובה יותר ככל שהטיטרציה במינון מהירה יותר
explanation:
Antidepressant benefit varies with the depressive syndrome and the clinical population. Symptoms such as apathy, withdrawal and poor appetite in dementia may have several causes.
**The average benefit of antidepressants for depression in dementia is uncertain, so define a treatment goal and reassess whether it is achieved.**

**A. Uncertain efficacy in dementia.** Negative trials limit confidence in a routine drug benefit. Caregiver support and tailored activities can improve mood and engagement.
**B. Negligible placebo response.** Many participants improve in placebo groups. This reduces the incremental effect attributable to the drug.
**C. Greater benefit in mild depression.** Evidence for added drug benefit is weaker at low symptom severity, especially for subsyndromal depression.
**D. Faster titration improves efficacy.** Gradual titration can improve adherence through fewer early adverse effects and closer contact. Faster escalation has no established advantage here.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1014–1015

q: מה ההבדלים בין זיהום ויראלי בשפעת INFLUENZA VIRUS לעומת RESPIRATORY SYNCYTIAL VIRUS (RSV)?
o: לשניהם תסמינים דומים, אך חום אופייני יותר בשפעת
RSV גורר פחות אשפוזים ביחס לשפעת
שפעת היא מחלה עונתית (חורף) וה- RSV לא
explanation:
Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus can both cause cough, breathlessness and worsening cardiopulmonary disease in older adults. Their symptoms overlap enough that testing may be needed to tell them apart.
**Fever is generally more pronounced with influenza, while wheezing can be more prominent with RSV.** Hospitalization burden varies with the population and season.

**A. Similar symptoms with fever more typical of influenza.** This is a useful pattern, although fever alone cannot diagnose the virus in an individual patient.
**B. Fewer admissions with RSV.** An earlier cohort had more influenza-related outpatient visits. That endpoint differs from admission, and later studies found similar or higher hospitalization rates with RSV.
**C. Only influenza is seasonal.** In temperate climates both typically circulate during the colder months.
**D. Oseltamivir treats both.** It is a neuraminidase inhibitor used for influenza A or B. It has no clinical role against RSV.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1736–1737.
Key note: Fewer RSV hospitalizations is also accepted, but Hazzard reports similar or higher RSV hospitalization rates in several studies of older adults.

q: אילו שינויים באנטומיה של הלב אופייניים לגיל מבוגר?
explanation:
Aging can be accompanied by **left atrial enlargement and a leftward electrical-axis shift**. Slower ventricular relaxation increases reliance on atrial filling. The axis is measured on ECG.

**A. Increased LV mass.** Wall thickening and remodeling are common, but total LV mass varies with body size, loading conditions and hypertension.
**B. Left atrial enlargement.** Chronic diastolic loading can increase left atrial size. Marked dilation warrants evaluation for disease.
**C. Leftward axis shift.** A leftward QRS axis is a common age-associated electrical finding, although the question calls it anatomical.
**D. Thin atrial septum.** The expected age-related pattern is thickening and stiffening.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 73, pp. 1118 and 1120–1121.

Key note: Left atrial enlargement is anatomical. A leftward electrical axis is an age-related ECG finding, so accepting it as an anatomical change makes the wording imprecise.

explanation:
Palliative wound treatment aims to relieve symptoms when a large, necrotic pressure wound is unlikely to close. Malodor can distress both the patient and people nearby.

**Apply topical metronidazole to the wound bed for odor.** An absorbent covering can contain drainage and reduce painful dressing changes.

**A. Povidone-iodine twice daily.** Repeated antiseptic dressings add handling and do not specifically target odor as effectively as the proposed symptom-directed treatment.
**B. Topical metronidazole.** Its activity against anaerobic organisms helps reduce malodor where it originates.
**C. Surgical debridement.** Removing necrosis can sometimes help smell or drain pus. Its procedural burden matters in a dying patient, and a topical option directly addresses the symptom.
**D. More frequent dressing changes.** Changing a saturated dressing is appropriate, but routinely increasing frequency can aggravate pain. Choose sufficient absorption and address the odor itself.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 697–698.

q: בת 78, אובחנה כסובלת מ- HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA. מה נכון לגבי האפשרויות הטיפוליות?
o: ניתוח לא הוכח כמשפר פרוגנוזה בקשישים
הסיכונים של transarterial chemoembolization דומים בצעירים ובמבוגרים

explanation:
Hepatocellular carcinoma treatment depends on stage, liver reserve and fitness. **Selected older and younger patients have similar complication rates with transarterial chemoembolization**, so age alone need not exclude TACE.

**A. No surgical benefit in older adults.** Resection can offer reasonable outcomes in appropriately selected older patients.
**B. Comparable TACE risks.** Patient selection, including hepatic reserve and tumor distribution, matters more than a universal age cutoff.
**C. Prefer kinase inhibition at any stage.** Systemic treatment for advanced disease does not routinely replace feasible surgery or locoregional therapy.
**D. Palliation alone because of age.** Consider active treatments in the context of tumor extent, health and preferences.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1448, 1449.

q: מהו הטיפול המועדף בגיל המבוגר שמפחית UREMIC PRURITIS במטופל עם אי ספיקת כליות, המטופל בהמודיאליזה ?
explanation:
Uremic pruritus can disturb sleep and cause excoriations in patients receiving hemodialysis. **Low-dose gabapentin** can reduce this itch after skin care, dialysis adequacy and other contributors have been addressed.

**A. Low-dose gabapentin** — Gabapentin has demonstrated benefit for dialysis-associated itch. Reduced renal clearance makes a low dose and review for sedation particularly important.
**B. Potassium and sodium phosphate** — Adding phosphate is not an antipruritic intervention. Phosphate control is part of the assessment, especially when phosphate is already elevated.
**C. Escitalopram** — This SSRI treats depression and anxiety. The symptom pattern here calls for treatment directed at uremic itch.
**D. Permethrin cream** — Permethrin treats scabies. A compatible infestation history or examination would be needed to choose it.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1296, Pruritus.

q: מה נכון לגבי טיפול ב- HFpEF ( HEART FAILURE WITH PRESERVED EJECTION FRACTION) ?
o: CANDESRATAN מוריד תמותה אך לא מוריד אשפוזים
explanation:
In HFpEF a trial can improve a composite outcome because one component falls. **Empagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization as a combined endpoint, mainly through fewer HF admissions**.

**A. Empagliflozin** This is the closest choice. Cardiovascular mortality alone was not significantly reduced in EMPEROR-Preserved, and the benefit extended to patients without diabetes.
**B. Candesartan** CHARM-Preserved showed fewer HF admissions without a demonstrated mortality benefit. The option reverses these outcomes.
**C. Beta blockers** Trials have not established a general HFpEF survival benefit. They may be indicated for another condition such as AF.
**D. Digoxin** The ancillary DIG study did not show a survival benefit. Routine digoxin for HFpEF is not supported.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1186–1188. EMPEROR-Preserved (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2107038).

Key note: The option implies separate reductions in admissions and mortality. The significant result was the composite, driven chiefly by fewer HF hospitalizations.

q: בת 78, סובלת מסוכרת ויתר לחץ דם. פנתה בשל חולשה גוברת וכאב בגפיים תחתונות. כשבועיים טרם פנייתה אובחן שלשול על רקע CAMPYLOBACTER JEJUNI והשלימה טיפול ב- CIPROFLOXACIN. מהי האבחנה הסבירה ביותר?
o: נוירופטיה הנגרמה על יד טיפול אנטיביוטי
explanation:
Guillain-Barré syndrome is an acute immune-mediated peripheral neuropathy. Progressively weak, painful limbs appearing one to three weeks after a diarrheal illness should prompt assessment of reflexes, breathing and autonomic function.
**Guillain-Barré syndrome best fits the progressive leg weakness two weeks after Campylobacter jejuni enteritis.**

**A. Antibiotic-induced neuropathy.** Fluoroquinolone-associated neuropathy is possible, but the characteristic antecedent infection and progressive motor syndrome more strongly suggest Guillain-Barré syndrome.
**B. Guillain-Barré syndrome.** Campylobacter is a well-recognized antecedent. Pain can accompany early weakness, and deep tendon reflexes often diminish as the illness evolves.
**C. Myasthenia gravis.** Fluctuating, fatigable weakness, often ocular or bulbar, is more characteristic. Painful progressive leg weakness after enteritis points elsewhere.
**D. Diabetic neuropathy.** Typical distal diabetic polyneuropathy develops gradually and is often sensory-predominant. The rapid course after infection is atypical.

Reference · Harrison, 21e, chapter 447, pp. 3501–3502.

q: איזו בדיקה יש לבצע בחולה עם RHEOMATOID ARTHRITIS לפני התחלת טיפול ב- ANTI-TNF?
explanation:
TNF is important in maintaining granulomas that contain tuberculosis. **Screen for latent tuberculosis before starting anti-TNF treatment**, using a tuberculin skin test or an appropriate interferon-gamma release assay together with clinical evaluation.

**A. Echocardiography.** It can be indicated for suspected heart failure but does not screen for latent TB.
**B. Pulmonary function tests.** Spirometry cannot detect latent tuberculosis.
**C. Coagulation studies.** They do not assess the infection risk specific to TNF blockade.
**D. Mantoux test.** This is a tuberculin skin test. A positive result requires assessment for active TB and a plan for latent infection before immunosuppression.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1617.

q: בן 82, התקבל למיון בשל בלבול חריף. בבדיקות המעבדה: קריאטינין 3 mg/dL, רמת סידן 11.5 mg/dL (תקין – 8.7-10.2 mg/dL), רמת PTH – 12pg/mL (תקין 15-65 pg/mL). איזו מהסיבות הבאות סביר להניח תהיה הגורם למצבו?
explanation:
Hypercalcemia should suppress parathyroid hormone. A PTH of 12 pg/mL with calcium of 11.5 mg/dL indicates a PTH-independent process. **Multiple myeloma is the strongest explanation for hypercalcemia accompanied by renal failure and acute confusion.**

**A. Hydrochlorothiazide** — Thiazides can elevate calcium by reducing its excretion. No exposure is given, and this is a less persuasive explanation for the full presentation.
**B. Primary hyperparathyroidism** — PTH is typically elevated or inappropriately normal for the calcium concentration.
**C. Tertiary hyperparathyroidism** — Longstanding severe secondary hyperparathyroidism can become autonomous, producing high PTH despite hypercalcemia.
**D. Multiple myeloma** — Osteolytic disease can raise calcium, suppress PTH and coexist with kidney injury. These clues warrant investigation for myeloma.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1538, Table 97-9.

q: מה מהבאים אופייני לרעד של מחלת פרקינסון?
explanation:
Tremor is classified by what the limb is doing when it appears. Observe the hand supported in the lap, then with the arms outstretched and during writing.

**Rest tremor is characteristic of Parkinson disease.** It is often most apparent in one supported hand early in the illness and may lessen during voluntary movement.

**A. Tremor at rest.** A tremor predominating when the limb is relaxed fits the parkinsonian pattern.
**B. Symmetric tremor.** Idiopathic Parkinson disease commonly starts on one side. Bilateral symmetric hand tremor is more typical of essential tremor.
**C. Worse with arms outstretched.** An increase while holding a posture favors a postural tremor, often seen in essential tremor.
**D. Worse while writing.** An increase during a task is a kinetic tremor. It is less characteristic of the predominant parkinsonian rest tremor.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 939–941.

q: מה נכלל בקריטריונים להשתלת CRT - CARDIAC RESYNCHRONIZATION THERAPY ?
o: אי ספיקת לב עם תפקוד סיסטולי EF% = 40
אי ספיקת לב מסוג HFpEF בחומרת NYHA IV
אי ספיקת לב מסוג HFrEF בחומרת NYHA III
explanation:
CRT uses biventricular pacing to correct delayed ventricular activation. **NYHA class III symptoms in HFrEF can form part of the indication**, alongside low EF, a suitable conduction pattern and persistent symptoms despite tolerated treatment.

**A. EF of 40%** A routine HFrEF resynchronization indication generally requires EF at or below 35%. Separate pacing indications are assessed differently.
**B. Class IV HFpEF** Advanced symptoms with preserved EF do not establish the usual HFrEF CRT indication.
**C. QRS duration of 120 ms** A value of 120 ms alone does not identify a CRT candidate. Benefit is strongest with LBBB and QRS at least 150 ms, with narrower ranges considered in selected cases.
**D. Class III HFrEF** This satisfies the symptom component. Confirm EF, QRS duration and morphology, rhythm, treatment and goals.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1184. AHA/ACC/HFSA HF guideline (2022), §7.4.1. ESC pacing and CRT guideline (2021), §6.3.

Key note: Hazzard gives a QRS threshold of 150 ms here. US guidance allows selected patients with LBBB and a QRS of 120–149 ms to qualify. The European pacing guideline excludes QRS below 130 ms in the absence of a separate pacing indication.

q: איזו מהפעולות הבאות במהלך השיקום אסורה בחולה לאחר החלפה מלאה של ירך בגישה אחורית?
explanation:
During early healing after a traditional posterior hip replacement, certain positions can dislocate the prosthetic joint. Crossing the legs brings the operated hip into adduction across the midline.

**Avoid sitting with one leg crossed over the other when posterior hip precautions are prescribed.**

**A. Sitting on a high chair.** A suitably raised seat reduces the hip flexion needed to sit down and stand up.
**B. Sitting with legs apart.** This keeps the thigh away from the cross-midline position of concern.
**C. Sitting with legs crossed.** Crossing brings the operated thigh inward. In early posterior precautions this is one of the positions avoided to reduce dislocation risk.
**D. Walking with full weight bearing.** Loading and hip position are separate postoperative instructions. Weight bearing may be permitted according to the surgeon’s plan.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 794, 832.

. Walking with full weight bearing.** Loading and hip position are separate postoperative instructions. Weight bearing may be permitted according to the surgeon’s plan.

During early healing after a traditional posterior hip replacement, certain positions can dislocate the prosthetic joint. Crossing the legs brings the operated hip into adduction across the midline.

**Avoid sitting with one leg crossed over the other when posterior hip precautions are prescribed.**

q: באיזה מהבאים מתוארת תופעת לוואי המתאימה לתרופה נגד עצירות הרשומה?
o: תמציות SENNA גורמות ל- MELANOSIS COLI
explanation:
Stimulant laxatives, osmotic agents and enemas have different adverse-effect patterns. Anthraquinone exposure is associated with a characteristic pigmentation of the colonic mucosa.
**Senna is associated with melanosis coli.**

**A. Senna and melanosis coli.** Anthraquinone laxatives can cause brown discoloration of the colonic lining. This finding alone is not evidence of myenteric nerve injury.
**B. Phosphate enema and low phosphate.** Absorbed phosphate can raise serum phosphate, particularly in renal impairment.
**C. Psyllium and sweet taste.** Psyllium commonly causes bloating or flatulence. A sweet taste is characteristic of lactulose or sorbitol.
**D. Bisacodyl and flatulence.** Cramping and rectal burning are more characteristic. Gas is more typical of fiber and fermentable osmotic agents.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Table 87-9, pp. 1373–1374.

q: איזה מהבאים הוא אחד הקריטריונים ל- COGNITIVE FRAILTY?
explanation:
Cognitive frailty describes the coexistence of physical frailty and cognitive impairment short of dementia. **Mild cognitive impairment is the required cognitive component.**

**A. Dementia** — The definition excludes Alzheimer disease and other dementias. Established dementia changes the clinical classification.
**B. Dependence in personal care** — Dependence measures disability. Physical frailty can precede dependence and must be assessed separately.
**C. Mild cognitive impairment** — The operational description uses a Clinical Dementia Rating of 0.5 alongside physical frailty, after exclusion of dementia.
**D. Depression** — Mood symptoms can influence energy and cognition and deserve assessment. Depression is not a defining component.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 627, Cognition, Dementia, and Frailty.

q: בת 84, ברקע יתר לחץ דם ואוסטראוארטריטיס. עשתה בדיקת דם שגרתית במרפאה. בבדיקה נמצאה רמת אשלגן 6.4. מה מהווה סיבה אפשרית להיפרקלמיה באשה זו?
explanation:
A high serum potassium can reflect potassium released during sample clotting. **Marked thrombocytosis can cause pseudohyperkalemia. A value of 6.4 warrants prompt clinical and ECG assessment and confirmation with an appropriately collected plasma sample.**

**A. Primary hyperaldosteronism** — Excess aldosterone increases renal potassium excretion and may produce hypokalemia.
**B. Thrombocytosis** — A high platelet count can raise potassium in serum during clotting while plasma potassium remains normal.
**C. Hypomagnesemia** — Magnesium depletion promotes renal potassium wasting and can make hypokalemia difficult to correct.
**D. Polydipsia** — Excess water intake predisposes to dilutional hyponatremia and does not account for this potassium result.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1270–1271, 1532–1533.

q: בן 72 פנה למיון עקב החמרה בקשיי הנשימה בשבוע האחרון, במיוחד בלילות. מציין שיעול והוצאת קצף מהפה בחודש האחרון. ידוע על יתר לחץ דם מזה תקופה ארוכה, סוכרת ואי ספיקת כליות כרונית, עישון של קופסה אחת ליום במשך 20 שנה. בבדיקתו: חום גוף תקין, 25 נשימות לדקה, לחץ דם 147/98, דופק 110 פעימות לדקה. ריאות: פצפוצים (CREPITATIONS) בבסיסי הריאות דו צדדית, לב: קול נוסף בסוף הדיאסטולה, עמום, בולט יותר בחוד הלב. ללא גודש וורידי הצוואר או בצקות ברגליים. מה הפתופיזיולוגיה שגרמה למצבו הנוכחי של החולה?
explanation:
A fourth heart sound occurs late in diastole as the atrium contracts into a poorly compliant ventricle. **Impaired relaxation with high filling pressure** best links the apical S4, longstanding hypertension and nocturnal pulmonary congestion.

**A. Alveolar wall destruction** Emphysema can cause dyspnea but does not explain a new S4 or this pattern of pulmonary edema.
**B. Impaired myocardial relaxation** Hypertensive ventricular remodeling can elevate left atrial and pulmonary venous pressures despite a preserved EF. Echo assesses the actual EF and diastolic function.
**C. Impaired contraction** Systolic dysfunction can coexist. A dilated ventricle, displaced apex or S3 would support it more directly.
**D. Inflammatory lung infiltration** Pneumonia may cause crackles, but the orthopnea, frothy sputum and S4 point toward a cardiac cause.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1175, Table 76-7.

q: מה מאפיין POST-CONCUSSIVE SYNDROME?
o: חומרת התסמינים קשורה לחומרת הפגיעה הראשונית
explanation:
After concussion, headache, dizziness, sleep disturbance and emotional or cognitive changes can persist beyond the acute injury. **Depression, anxiety and subtle personality changes fit this syndrome.** A mild initial injury can still produce substantial lasting symptoms.

**A. Prolonged nausea and vomiting.** Persistent vomiting warrants reassessment for an acute complication, rather than attribution to an uncomplicated recovery.
**B. Symptom severity follows initial injury severity.** Record the severity of the injury and subsequent symptoms separately. Initial severity does not reliably determine who develops the syndrome or how disabling symptoms will be.
**C. Emotional and personality changes.** These can coexist with impaired concentration, fatigue and sleep disruption.
**D. Uncommon in older adults.** A prospective cohort of adults aged 55 and older with mild brain injury found persistent, life-affecting symptoms in 16% at 90 days. The estimate depends on age group, follow-up and symptom definition.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 995. Post-Concussion Symptoms in Older Adults Following a Mild Traumatic Brain Injury, PMID 40531474.

Hazzard lists the latter and says initial injury severity does not directly predict development of the postconcussive syndrome. The printed passage does not establish the proposed severity relationship.

q: מהו המאפיין הקליני הזהה ב- LATE ONSET RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS וב- YOUNG ONSET RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS?
o: בשתי המחלות היארעות גבוהה יותר בנשים לעומת גברים
בשתי המחלות אם RHEUMATOID FACTOR (RF) חיובי המחלה תהיה קשה יותר
בשתי המחלות ברוב החולים RF שלילי
בשתי המחלות יש שכיחות גבוהה של RHEUMATOID NODULES
explanation:
The clinical pattern of rheumatoid arthritis can vary with the age at onset. **A positive rheumatoid factor is associated with a more severe course in both late-onset and younger-onset rheumatoid arthritis.** This is a prognostic association, not a certainty for every individual.

**A. Higher incidence in women in both groups.** Younger-onset disease generally shows female predominance. In late-onset disease men and women are affected at roughly similar rates. The exact ratio varies across populations, so a female excess is not a dependable shared feature.
**B. Positive RF predicts a more severe course.** Seropositivity has prognostic significance in both onset groups and is interpreted with the clinical findings.
**C. Most patients are RF-negative in both.** RF negativity is more characteristic of some late-onset presentations. It is not a majority rule applicable to both groups.
**D. Rheumatoid nodules are frequent in both.** Nodules are less characteristic of late-onset disease.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1608, 1610, Table 101-2.

q: בת 83, פונה בשל תחושת סחרחורת כשעה לאחר ארוחת הצהריים. איזו תופעה פיזיולוגית גורמת לבעיה ממנה סובלת המטופלת?
o: אפקט וזוקונסטריקטורי של אינסולין על כלי הדם של מערכת העיכול
explanation:
An older adult who becomes dizzy about an hour after lunch may have postprandial hypotension. **Pooling of blood in the splanchnic circulation** reduces venous return, especially when the compensatory increase in vascular resistance is inadequate.

**A. Increased venous return** — The post-meal shift of blood toward the gastrointestinal circulation reduces central filling.
**B. Reduced parasympathetic activity** — Vagal withdrawal can support a higher heart rate. The more relevant failure is insufficient sympathetic compensation.
**C. Insulin constricts gastrointestinal vessels** — Insulin and gut peptides can have vasodilator effects after eating.
**D. Splanchnic pooling** — Redistribution to the gut and an inadequate vascular response can lower pressure. Measurements before and after a meal can document the fall.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 668.

q: איזה מהמשפטים הבאים מתאר נכון טיפול בנזק אפשרי לבלוטת התריס משימוש ב- AMIODARONE?
o: במקרה של היפרתירואידיזם קשה המצריך הפסקת AMIODARONE יש צפי לשיפור משמעותי בתפקודי התריס לאחר שבועיים
עלייה ב- TSH שבועיים לאחר התחלת טיפול ב- AMIODARONE מחייבת הפסקה של התרופה
תירוטוקסיקוזיס במנגנון של DESTRUCTIVE THYROIDITIS מגיב לטיפול בסטרואידים
מטופלים עם רקע של מחלת GRAVES נמצאים בסיכון מוגבר להיפותירואידיזם תחת טיפול ב- AMIODARONE ויזדקקו לטיפול בהורמון תירואיד
explanation:
Amiodarone can injure thyroid cells and cause stored hormone to leak into the circulation. **Corticosteroids treat this destructive thyroiditis.**

**A. Expect recovery two weeks after stopping** The long half-life, tissue accumulation and iodine load mean amiodarone effects can persist for months.
**B. Stop for an early TSH rise** A transient rise shortly after starting can occur with a normal underlying gland and usually needs observation.
**C. Steroids for destructive thyroiditis** The target is inflammation and cell injury. Blocking new hormone synthesis alone misses release of preformed hormone.
**D. Graves disease predicts deficiency** Underlying Graves disease or autonomous nodular tissue predisposes to increased synthesis. Hypothyroidism is more typical with underlying Hashimoto disease.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1547–1548, Amiodarone and thyroid function.

q: בן 78, אובחן כחולה במחלת פרקינסון, שמתבטאת בעצירות ורעד ביד ימין המשפעים על איכות חייו. באיזו מהתרופות הבאות מומלץ להתחיל?
explanation:
Levodopa is a dopamine precursor that can enter the brain and relieve parkinsonian motor symptoms. A peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor such as carbidopa limits conversion before levodopa reaches the brain.

**Start levodopa with a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor for the troublesome motor symptoms.** At age 78 it has a more favorable balance of motor efficacy and neuropsychiatric tolerability than a dopamine agonist.

**A. Amantadine.** Its principal role is as an adjunct, especially for levodopa-induced dyskinesia. It can provoke confusion and hallucinations in older adults.
**B. Pramipexole.** This agonist can improve movement, but hallucinations, confusion and sleepiness are more common than with levodopa.
**C. Levodopa.** It is the most effective oral motor treatment and can improve a parkinsonian tremor. The constipation also deserves its own assessment and treatment.
**D. Entacapone.** It prolongs the effect of levodopa and is useful when benefit wears off. It requires levodopa to act as an adjunct.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 939, 943–944, 948.

o: חולשה, ירידה לא מכוונת במשקל, מיעוט בפעילות, תשישות
חולשה, איטיות, BMI (body Mass Index) קטן מ-21, מיעוט בפעילות
חולשה, איטיות פסיכומוטורית, ירידה תפקודית, מצב רוח ירוד
איטיות, BMI קטן מ-21 או גבוה מ-30, מיעוט בפעילות, ירידה קוגניטיבית
explanation:
Fried’s phenotype includes weakness, unintentional weight loss, low activity, exhaustion and slow gait. **Weakness, unintentional weight loss, low activity and exhaustion are all genuine components.**

**A. Weakness, weight loss, low activity and exhaustion** — All four belong to the phenotype. The fifth component is objectively slow walking.
**B. Weakness, slowness, BMI below 21 and low activity** — A single low BMI is not equivalent to losing weight unintentionally. BMI helps interpret grip thresholds.
**C. Psychomotor slowing, functional decline and low mood** — The phenotype uses timed gait and self-reported exhaustion. Broad decline and depressed mood do not replace these measures.
**D. BMI outside a range and cognitive decline** — Both very low and very high BMI can accompany frailty, but neither BMI extremes nor cognition are scored as phenotype components.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 619–620, Table 42-2.

q: לאיזה מהבאים יש קורלציה גבוהה עם TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY?
explanation:
Traumatic brain injury may precede persistent cognitive decline or hydrocephalus. **Secondary posttraumatic hydrocephalus can resemble normal pressure hydrocephalus. The association with later dementia is clearer than a specific link to Alzheimer pathology**.

**A. Alzheimer disease.** Dementia after injury has several potential causes and cannot be equated with Alzheimer disease.
**B. Normal pressure hydrocephalus.** Disrupted CSF circulation after trauma can produce gait, urinary and cognitive symptoms.
**C. ALS.** An early association may reflect falls during emerging motor disease. A sustained causal link is uncertain.
**D. Meningioma.** Reported observational associations do not demonstrate that trauma caused an individual tumor.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 997, and Yoon et al., Korean Journal of Neurotrauma 2018, pp. 86–92.
Key note: Both Alzheimer disease and normal pressure hydrocephalus received credit. Hazzard describes cohort and autopsy studies finding no specific association with an Alzheimer diagnosis or pathology.

q: בן 77, צלול ועצמאי, הגיע מביתו. ברקע ידוע על Ulcerative Colitis (UC) מזה כ- 15 שנים. המטופל הגיע כדי לשאול לגבי צורך בקולונוסקופיה למעקב. מציין שפעם אחרונה שעשה היה לפני כשנתיים, אז היה תקין. מה נכון לגבי הצורך במעקב?
o: מאחר והסבירות לממאירות ב- Ulcerative Colitis נמוכה יותר ביחס ל- Chron’s Disease, בדיקה חוזרת כל 5 שנים
מאחר וחלפו מעל 10 שנים מתחילת המחלה בדיקה חוזרת אחת ל- 1-3 שנים
מאחר וגילו מעל 75 שנים אין אינדיקציה להמשך מעקב קולונוסקופיה
מאחר והסיכון לממאירות מעל 50%, בדיקה חוזרת כל חצי שנה
explanation:
Long-standing ulcerative colitis increases colorectal neoplasia risk. After 15 years of disease, **surveillance colonoscopy at roughly one- to three-year intervals** is the interval described here, individualized to risk and health.

**A. Every five years for lower risk.** Ulcerative colitis and extensive Crohn colitis can both carry appreciable colorectal cancer risk.
**B. Every one to three years.** Surveillance begins around eight to ten years after onset in colonic disease, fitting this duration.
**C. Stop at 75.** Age alone should not decide surveillance in an independent patient with long-standing disease.
**D. Every six months.** Neither a blanket risk above 50% nor this frequency follows from the reported duration and normal prior examination.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1309.

q: בן 85, מתגורר בביתו עם מטפל צמוד בעקבות דמנציה וצורך בהשגחה. מתהלך ללא אביזר עזר. מאושפז בעקבות אירוע מוחי נרחב בטריטוריה של MCA, פלגיה מימין ואפזיה מעורבת. במהלך האשפוז אירועי אספירציה, טופל באנטיביוטיקה, מוזן דרך זונדה. בפיזיותרפיה לא מבין הוראות. לא מבצע פקודות פשוטות. מעברים במנוף. משפחתו מבקשת להעבירו למסגרת שיקומית. מה הגורם השולל התאמת המטופל לשיקום על פי נוהל אמות מידה למתן טיפול שיקומי לקשישים?
explanation:
שיקום דורש השתתפות מספקת בתרגול. אחרי שבץ עם אפזיה בודקים אם המטופל מצליח לפעול גם בעזרת הדגמה, מחוות והנחיות פשוטות.

**המגבלה הקובעת כאן היא חוסר היכולת לשתף פעולה בפועל. בפיזיותרפיה הוא אינו מבצע אפילו פקודה פשוטה, ולכן קשה בשלב זה לבנות אימון פעיל שאפשר לחזור עליו.**

**A. מגורים קודמים עם מטפל.** עזרה קודמת מגדירה את נקודת המוצא ואת פוטנציאל התמיכה. לפני השבץ הוא התהלך ללא אביזר עזר.
**B. הזנה בזונדה.** אפשר לשלב הזנה בזונדה עם שיקום כאשר מצב ההזנה והנשימה מאפשר טיפול בטוח.
**C. מעברים במנוף.** הצורך במנוף מתאר את חומרת התלות הנוכחית. הוא אינו מלמד כשלעצמו אם המטופל מסוגל ללמוד ולהשתתף.
**D. חוסר יכולת לשתף פעולה.** הקושי הודגם במהלך טיפול. מעריכים מחדש אם התקשורת או היכולת לבצע הוראות משתפרות.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, חוזר מינהל רפואה 4/2009, סעיפים 5.2–5.3, עמ׳ 4.
